text:
ana: heads up — multiple customers opened escalations 30m ago about p95/p99 spikes for chat endpoints. seeing sustained p95 ~2.2s (expected ~350ms) and p99 > 4s on prod-us-west, coinciding with yesterday's deployment of cache_v2 eviction tweak.

sam: ack. are these correlated to model variant or specific routes?

ana: most reports are on gpt-small-v1 route and on workloads with many short prompts (conversational assistants). also bumped from ~60% kv cache hit -> ~12% in metrics.

mike: that sounds like cache thrash. I pulled the recent telemetry:
```
# kv/cache metrics (prod-us-west, 10m window)
kv_cache_hits: 1.2k
kv_cache_misses: 9.1k
cache_evictions: 8.6k
avg_cache_latency_ms: 7.3
cache_occupancy_pct: 82
```
looks like eviction rate spiked after eviction-policy change -> LRU->approx-LRU with micro-buckets.

lina: any obvious cache key churn? can we repro locally?

ana: found diff in key composer in last PR -> we started including request.user_metadata in prefix keys to support per-tenant routing. example bad key: `model:gpt-small-v1|prefix_hash:0xabc|user_meta:{"tenant_tier":"beta","session_id":"s-12345"}`. session_id is unique per request -> essentially disabling reuse.

sam: yikes. that would definitely create near-zero reuse for short prompts. Is that change in canary config only or full rollout?

ana: full rollout to prod yesterday. rollout script shows config applied to all clusters at 21:17 UTC.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) revert key composer to strip ephemeral fields (session_id, request_id) 2) roll back eviction-policy change to previous LRU buckets 3) enlarge cache pool temporarily for affected clusters 4) pre-warm prefixes for top-100 prompt prefixes.

lina: agree. add immediate customer-facing workaround: tell affected customers to set `client.cacheable_prefix=true` and avoid sending opaque session_id in metadata for a few hours — support-bot can DM template.

ana: I've prepared minimal patch to sanitize key parts (PR ready). snippet: 
```
function normalize_meta(meta) {
  delete meta.session_id;
  delete meta.request_id;
  return pick(meta, ['tenant_tier','region']);
}
cache_key = `${model}|prefix:${prefix_hash}|meta:${hash(normalize_meta(meta))}`;
```
will push to hotfix branch after approvals.

mike: can we hot-restart cache process without full deploy? infra-bot: any rolling config apply path?

infra-bot: we have a feature-flag path. can flip key_composer=v1 -> v2-safe with zero-downtime and gradual canary. will take ~8m per cluster.

sam: good. do that asap. also schedule canary to 10% for 30m, watch p95 and kv hit rate. if kv_hit_rate > 50% and p95 < 500ms -> roll to 100%.

ana: also adding an emergency guarding rule: if eviction_rate > 5000/min then pause writes to cache (serve with cold runs) to avoid thrash loop. adding monitoring alert.

mike: lets also patch eviction policy to prefer TTL-first for small-sequence entries. we'll open a follow-up to convert to LFU or hybrid (LFU+TTL) — LFU prevents recent-large-burst items from evicting frequently accessed prefixes.

lina: for reproducible tests: create a load generator that mimics short prompt mixes and includes noisy metadata. run against stage with both old and new key composer to measure hit rates. I'll take it.

ana: repro steps I'm putting in the issue:
- curl traffic sim script (attached) that sends 10k requests across 200 distinct session_ids and only 25 unique prompt prefixes
- measure kv.hit / kv.miss and p95 token latencies
- expected: with broken composer hit < 15% and p95 > 1.5s; with sanitized composer hit > 60% and p95 ~350ms

support-bot: customer response template prepared: "we're rolling a fix to address cache key noise causing latency regressions. temporary workaround: avoid sending ephemeral session_id in the metadata or use the `cacheable_prefix` flag. ETA for staged fix: ~45-90 minutes."

mike: timeline: flip safe composer to 10% canary now -> 1743105750 (in ~6m). if metrics improve, progressively 25/50/100 over next 40m. hotfix PR -> review @sam @lina. if revert needed, infra-bot will flip key_composer back.

sam: I reviewed PR and left 1 comment about unit tests for normalize_meta — please add edge-case for nested session_id in strings.

ana: will add tests. pushing hotfix in 3m.

infra-bot: canary flip started for cluster-prod-us-west-1 -> 10% at 1743105780.

observability-bot: alert suppressed for 1h while mitigation in progress.

mike: keep thread updated with metrics. if anyone sees odd behavior (increased 5xx or cache corruption) pause immediately.

lina: after fix shipped, followups: add stricter lint rule preventing ephemeral fields in cache keys, add dashboard for cache churn (per-prefix cardinality), and a migration doc for eviction policies.

ana: filing ENG-1248 with full context + repro + PR link. assigning to me for the hotfix.

support-bot: I've notified the 3 affected customers with the template and given ETA. will update when fix completes. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks team. good catch catching metadata churn early. postmortem please if this impacts many customers.

mike: once p95 stable for 30m we'll close the incident and start retrospective.
